would_have_shipped_defects.evidence: artefacts/scripts/hive-tooling-drill.sh:190 (`tmux new-window -d -t "$TMUX_SESSION:4" -n occupied-slot -c "$WS_ROOT"`) against `set -euo pipefail` at line 24; WS_ROOT appears nowhere else in the file (grep: single hit at 190); candidate.patch:76
would_have_shipped_defects.summary: The new drill case dereferences an undefined variable ($WS_ROOT) under `set -u`, so the drill aborts at the first new line and every assertion from that point on — the two new cases plus all existing lifecycle, throttle, adopt and refusal checks — never runs.
would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: scripts/hive-tooling-drill.sh sets `set -euo pipefail` (line 24). WS_ROOT is defined only inside hive-launch, never in the drill's own shell (the drill exports HIVE_TMUX_SESSION, WS_HUB, OPS_WS, CANON_ROOT, WORK_ROOT, WRAPPER_DIR at lines 151-157, and never sources hive-common.sh in the main shell). The operator who runs the drill against the green cell — the exact hand-off the rubric describes — gets `hive-tooling-drill.sh: line 190: WS_ROOT: unbound variable` and a non-zero exit immediately after the alpha-demo launch section. Confirmed by running the same construct: `set -euo pipefail; foo -c "$WS_ROOT"` exits 1 with `WS_ROOT: unbound variable`. Both order scope item 4 clauses fail: the occupied-index case and the half-launch recovery assertion never execute, and the existing assertions do not stay green. The 'after' half of the reproduction evidence, which the report defers to this operator run, is therefore unreachable. bash -n and shellcheck cannot catch this class (both verifier logs are empty/clean), so it would have reached the operator undetected.

would_have_shipped_defects.why_blocking: Order scope item 2 requires an open window already named for this task to be 'refused with an error that names the recovery path, never a second window'. The refusal at hive-launch:137 dies with `a tmux window named '$TASK' already exists in session '$HIVE_TMUX_SESSION' (the pane is the registry)` — it states the rule but gives the operator no path forward, unlike the sibling refusals in the same script which do (`recover via task.reassigned (RUNBOOK)`, hive-launch:119/122). The candidate patch does not touch this line, and the RUNBOOK addition covers only the half-launch case, so an operator hitting a name collision is left to archaeology — the failure mode this order exists to remove. The report asserts the fix 'keep[s] the existing name-collision refusal' as if the leg were closed, which overstates what is there.
